name: a citation loop leaves a partial order and a reported cycle
why: a -> b -> c -> a is a loop. a also cites base, top cites a, side cites base. Kahn's algorithm places what it can and reports the rest instead of failing; the reading path keeps the loop together.

queries.why: base links to nothing and goes first; that frees side. a still waits on b, b on c, c on a, and top on a, so those four are unplaced: the loop and everything citing into it.
Sorted IDs are a, b, base, c, side, top. The loop holds the smallest ID a, so it is component 0.
From a the search tries b before base (ID order), then c, whose link to a meets a grey node.
top reaches a, b, c and base. The loop collapses into one group that depends on base, so base comes first, then the loop in ID order, then top.
When the target is on the loop, its group is last and the target is moved to the end of the group: a, c, then b.
